114: If the city is either longer than it is wide or it is square but not oriented with the cardinal directions, because there are still four even corners, when measuring the two thousand amot of the city's techum, we live it as it is and measure two thousand amot in each of the four directions.

If [the city] is round, we make corners and imagine it as if it were within the square. We then measure from the sides of this square two thousand amot in each direction, meaning that it gains the the corners. Similarly, if the city is triangular or has many sides, we make it into a square and then we measure two thousand amot from each side of the square.
when making it into a square, one should align it with the world such that each direction will be orthogonal to a cardinal direction and will be aligned with them.
